clue.text: One conservative in Far Eastern country rejected party

indicators.note: 'in' places the first pieces inside the country's name
something rejected is sent back, so the whole build is read from the end

blocks.note: Laos is a country in South-East Asia
the Roman numeral for one
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A lone Tory living in an Asian state turns down an invitation to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: I and C go inside LAOS to make LAICOS, which read backwards is SOCIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is an informal gathering or get-together, a noun synonym for a party.

clue.text: European characters from Brussels love Neighbours

indicators.note: the answer is made of consecutive letters taken straight out of the following words

blocks.note: the run of letters across the end of Brussels, all of love and the start of Neighbours

explanation.surface: Belgian viewers fall for the Australian soap Neighbours.
explanation.walkthrough: Neighbours is a long-running Australian TV soap, popular in Britain; it is only a source of letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: A Slovene is a native of Slovenia, a nation in central Europe, so a European person.

clue.text: Agent in court behaved furtively

indicators.note: 'in' puts the agent inside the abbreviation for court

blocks.note: CT is the standard abbreviation for court
a rep is a sales representative, an agent

explanation.surface: A spy in the courtroom acted shiftily.
explanation.definitionFit: To creep is to move stealthily; the past tense crept matches the past-tense phrase about acting by stealth.

clue.text: Analgesic distributed in Paris

indicators.note: distributed letters are spread around and dealt out in a new arrangement

blocks.note: the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A painkiller handed out in the French capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is a common painkilling drug, and an analgesic is any medicine that relieves pain.

clue.text: Snatch sailor approaching Channel

blocks.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common crossword sailor
a duct is a channel or tube carrying fluid

explanation.surface: A seaman nearing the English Channel is grabbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Approaching' just places the sailor before the channel.
explanation.definitionFit: To abduct is to carry someone off by force, the same verb sense as to snatch a person.

clue.text: Cases for silk underwear?

blocks.note: first meaning: a silk is a senior barrister (Queen's or King's Counsel), and the cases handed to a barrister are called this
second meaning: close-fitting underpants

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it suggests silk lingerie in a box; in British legal slang a 'silk' is a senior barrister, who wears a silk gown.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister's instructions for a case are documents called by this name, and the same word means short underpants.

clue.text: Poor clue adjudged to be corrupted

indicators.note: a poor version is badly formed, so these letters must be put into a better order

blocks.note: the four letters to rearrange
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: A crossword critic decides a weak clue has gone rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulcerated tissue has open sores and is festering, so it has been corrupted in the old sense of decayed.

clue.text: Office worker distressed at delay

indicators.note: distressed suggests being upset and disturbed, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A clerk gets upset about being held up.
explanation.walkthrough: A tea lady was a woman employed in British offices to bring round tea, often late, as the surface hints.
explanation.definitionFit: The tea lady was a staff member who served hot drinks in a workplace, so a kind of office employee.

clue.text: Particular party to which Julie belonged may be reformed

indicators.note: something reformed is remade in a new shape, so these letters are rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: the thirteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A political party that Julie once joined could be reorganised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks political, but it means a celebration; the fiftieth-anniversary event is one specific kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A golden jubilee marks fifty years, an occasion for a celebration, so it is one particular kind of festivity.

clue.text: Words written to court mean nothing to landlord

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis scoring
a landlord lets property, so is a letter

explanation.surface: Legal documents sent to a court count for nothing with the property owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' here is the verb, to woo, not a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: A love letter is a written message sent to woo a sweetheart, which is what courting means.

clue.text: Small-town travellin' agents in place shortly

indicators.note: 'in' sets the travelling and the agents inside the short form of place

blocks.note: PL is the short form of place, as in street names
roving is travelling; the apostrophe drops the final G here as it does in the clue word
the CIA is the US intelligence agency, full of agents

explanation.surface: Travelling salesmen in a provincial spot, written in folksy shorthand.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped G of travellin' is the setter's signal to drop the G of the synonym too.
explanation.definitionFit: Provincial describes life outside the capital, often with a narrow outlook, matching the adjective small-town.

clue.text: See 9
Delay agreement about return of right match official

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the next words are read backwards
'about' means going round, so the agreement wraps the reversed pieces

blocks.note: a deal is an agreement
R is the abbreviation for right
a ref is a referee

explanation.surface: An agreement held up over the comeback of the right referee.
explanation.definitionFit: A deferral is a postponement, a noun synonym for delay.

clue.text: Single perversion brought about senator's decline

indicators.note: a perversion twists something out of its proper form, so the letters are turned round
brought about means placed around, so the scrambled word wraps the other piece

blocks.note: the six letters to rearrange
Sen. is the abbreviation for senator; the 's is the verb 'is' and gives nothing

explanation.surface: A lone act of perversion caused a politician's downfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Lessening means becoming smaller or reducing, and decline as a noun is a gradual fall or reduction.

clue.text: In backward places a fly becomes inactive

indicators.note: backward means the word for places runs from right to left
'In' puts the following words inside the reversed word

blocks.note: to set is to place, so places is sets
taken as written
a gnat is a small fly

explanation.surface: In remote spots, an insect falls dormant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward places' suggests underdeveloped regions, but places is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagnate is to stop flowing or developing, which is to go sluggish or idle.

clue.text: Stop tenor coming in, for example

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: say is used for 'for example', as in 'a fruit, say, an apple'
T is the abbreviation for tenor in music

explanation.surface: Halt the tenor's entrance, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to remain or stop somewhere, as in stop the night, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Earl given away by worthless fellow

indicators.note: something given away leaves its owner, so a letter is lost from the next word

blocks.note: cheap means of little value
E is the abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: A nobleman betrayed by a good-for-nothing man.
explanation.definitionFit: Chap is informal British for a man, the same everyday sense as fellow.

clue.text: His job depends on mine

blocks.note: surface reading: someone's employment rests on the speaker's, a colleague or subordinate
setter's reading: mine is a pit for digging coal, so this worker's living comes from one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' reads as the possessive pronoun, but it is the noun, a coal pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A collier is a coal miner, whose work exists only because the pit does.

clue.text: Habit male discarded, laid-back under guard

indicators.note: discarded means thrown out, so a letter is removed from the habit word
'back' after laid tells us to read that word in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a custom is a habit
M is the abbreviation for male
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monk's habit is shed, and he is relaxed while in detention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid-back' looks like one word meaning relaxed, but it splits into laid and a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Custodial means held in custody, as in a custodial sentence, so being under guard.

clue.text: Brewing tank turns up near dilapidated Greek bar

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the word is read from bottom to top
a dilapidated thing has fallen apart, so its letters are rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: a vat is a large vessel used in brewing
the four letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A brewery tank appears near a run-down Greek tavern.
explanation.definitionFit: A taverna is a small Greek restaurant or tavern, an eating and drinking place.

clue.text: What a test begins with keeps a learner perplexed

indicators.note: something that keeps another holds it inside

blocks.note: a cricket Test match starts with the captains tossing a coin: a toss
taken as written
L is for learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: An exam's opening question holds a student who is baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test' suggests an exam, but it is a Test match in cricket, which begins with a coin toss to decide who bats.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at a loss is an idiom for being puzzled and not knowing what to do.

clue.text: Little fish from river pinched by fairies

indicators.note: something pinched is gripped on both sides, so it sits inside the other word

blocks.note: elves are fairy folk
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Tiny fish stolen from a stream by the little people.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvers are young eels, small fish that swim up rivers.

clue.text: Welsh rugby team backs sick after p-passage

indicators.note: 'backs' means the word for sick goes into reverse
'after' says the sick piece comes second, following the passage piece

blocks.note: a passage is a lane, and the stutter in p-passage tells us to repeat its first letter
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A Welsh side falters, feeling queasy after a stammering spell.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammered p-passage means the synonym is stammered too.
explanation.definitionFit: Llanelli is a town in south Wales famous for its rugby union club, the Scarlets.

clue.text: Fresh meat cut into by sailors

indicators.note: something cut into has another piece pushed inside it

blocks.note: veal is calf meat
the RN, Royal Navy, is full of sailors

explanation.surface: Fresh meat being carved by seamen.
explanation.definitionFit: Vernal means belonging to spring, so youthful and new, which is a poetic sense of fresh.

clue.text: Some contrary people persuaded to drive off

indicators.note: 'Some' means only part of the following words is used, as a consecutive run
contrary means going the opposite way, so the run is read backwards

blocks.note: the run of letters across the end of people and start of persuaded

explanation.surface: A few awkward folk were talked into chasing someone away.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel is to drive back or ward off an attacker, the same as drive off.

clue.text: Stars having a lot to put up with? Far from it

indicators.note: 'Far from it' denies what came before, so the amount is swapped for its opposite

blocks.note: the opposite of a lot is little
to bear is to put up with

explanation.surface: Celebrities who have so much to tolerate? Not at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'having a lot to bear'; the denial turns this into having little to bear.
explanation.definitionFit: The Little Bear, Ursa Minor, is a constellation, a group of stars containing the Pole Star.

clue.text: Mere indoor sport

blocks.note: first meaning: a mere is a small lake
second meaning: a cue game played on a table, a relative of billiards

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mere' looks like the adjective meaning only, but it is the noun for a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small body of still water and the table game played with cues and balls.

clue.text: Fight is eclipsed by all others

indicators.note: something eclipsed is covered over, so it sits inside the other word

blocks.note: the rest means all the others
taken as written

explanation.surface: A contest overshadowed by every other one.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to oppose or struggle against, a verb synonym for to fight.

clue.text: Sorry about everything going west in TV series!

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so one word surrounds the other
in an across entry, going west means travelling right to left

blocks.note: sorry can mean sad, as in a sorry state
all means everything

explanation.surface: An apology over everything going wrong in a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going west' also suggests going wrong, a fitting nod to the Texas setting of the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Dallas was a long-running American TV drama about the oil-rich Ewing family of Texas.
